stem: A client with bronchial asthma has a new prescription for propranolol. Which finding should the nurse identify before administration?

options.A: Propranolol is contraindicated in bronchial asthma
options.B: Asthma makes propranolol more effective and requires a higher dose
options.C: Bronchial asthma has no relevance to propranolol therapy
options.D: Propranolol is specifically indicated to treat acute bronchospasm

rationale: The current propranolol label lists bronchial asthma as a contraindication. It also warns that propranolol may provoke a bronchial asthmatic attack by blocking beta-receptor-mediated bronchodilation.
educational_objective: Recognize bronchial asthma as a labeled contraindication to propranolol.
source_claim_supported: Propranolol is contraindicated in bronchial asthma and may provoke a bronchial asthmatic attack.
blueprint_locator: 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan, Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies, printed p.12 / PDF p.16
correction_summary: Removed the unsupported propranolol-versus-metoprolol comparison and tested the current propranolol label directly.
audit_findings: A is explicitly listed in the label. B–D contradict the contraindication/warning. No second answer remains.
